subject: Delta Enterprise - Request for fallback / feature commitment for contract
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@deltaenterprise.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Delta Enterprise - request: fallback model + SLA commitment for signed SOW

Team —

Delta (Emily + Kevin copied) are asking for two items before signing: 1) an explicit fallback policy that guarantees automatic downgrade to a smaller model within <200ms extra tail latency if our primary large model is unavailable, and 2) an SLA note in the SOW for 99.8% inference availability for their production tenant for the first 12 months. They want this committed before DocuSign.

Context: deal is in final legal review, revenue uplift ~ $2.1M ARR if we include a 12-month managed SLA addendum. Emily attached a draft SOW; I attached a snapshot of the capacity ask (capacity_estimate.xlsx).

Ask: Product & Eng — can we:
- confirm a fallback model + observable fallback trace (trace-id correlation) that we can promise in SOW
- outline operational controls and a realistic ETA to enable this for their tenant (with runbook references)

If we can reasonably commit to the fallback + a scoped SLA (with escape clauses around force majeure / major infra incidents), Sales will push signature today.

Thanks — Tessa
--
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@deltaenterprise.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta Enterprise - request: fallback model + SLA commitment for signed SOW

Tessa — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Quick clarifying Qs before I scope:
1) When you say "fallback model" do you mean a pinned smaller model variant (quantized) in the same region, or an automated route to our multi-region lower-capacity tier?
2) Is Delta willing to accept a ~30% reduction in per-inference quality (we should quantify with 50 example prompts) for the fallback period, or do they expect parity?
3) For the SLA, do they need historical traces/telemetry retained beyond standard retention (they've mentioned audit requirements) — if so we need to flag retention/obs costs.

If we get answers to the above, I can propose a product-scoped commitment and an ETA. My instinct: we can offer a deterministic fallback (model pin + KV cache warming) and an SLA with conditional exclusions. But to be safe I'll lean towards a 2-week enablement window after signature for the full observability hooks.

—Priyom
Principal PM, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@deltaenterprise.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta Enterprise - request: fallback model + SLA commitment for signed SOW

Priyom / Tessa — technical take from infra/serving:
- Feasibility: We can implement a pinned fallback variant (gptx-medium-quant) in the same region and route automatically when primary model endpoints start failing health checks or queueing beyond a latency threshold.
- Observability: We can inject a trace_id header and a fallback_flag metric; both are existing hooks in the runtime, so low-code on our side.
- Risk/Tradeoffs: Fallback will reduce average quality on some prompts; we should include an acceptance test suite (50 prompts) in the SOW to set expectations. There is a non-zero risk during cold-starts for the fallback instance — recommend pre-warming.
- ETA and effort: scoped work: 4 engineer-days to wire the routing + telemetry + a runbook; 2 additional days for QA and the acceptance suite. Ops support to onboard Delta tenant: 3 person-days. Total: ~9 person-days. If prioritized, we can target enablement within 10 business days post-signature.

I'll attach a short capacity sketch after lunch.

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@deltaenterprise.com>, Kevin Luo <kevin.luo@deltaenterprise.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta Enterprise - request: fallback model + SLA commitment for signed SOW

Folks —

Delta is at the legal finish line. They need the fallback + SLA to be explicitly called out so their procurement can sign off. From a commercial perspective we can offer:
- the fallback guarantee as a feature-level commitment (as described by Dev)
- the SLA at 99.8% for the tenant for 12 months, with exclusions for major cloud outages and scheduled maintenance (we'll put a 72-hour notification clause)

In exchange, Delta will commit to the 12-month term and approve a 10% increase in the committed throughput baseline (this gives us buffer capacity). They are agreeable to the acceptance suite and will provide 50 representative prompts by Friday.

We need product to ack the service description language (SOW wording) and confirm the 10-business-day enablement is acceptable. Legal wants the exact runbook reference (or a link) to include in the SOW.

Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@deltaenterprise.com>, Kevin Luo <kevin.luo@deltaenterprise.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta Enterprise - request: fallback model + SLA commitment for signed SOW

Ben / Team — confirming product stance and proposed SOW language so legal can move:

1) Feature commitment: For the duration of the SOW, Redwood will provide an automated fallback route that routes incoming inference requests to a pre-specified, regional, lower-capacity model variant when the primary model endpoint violates health or latency thresholds. Redwood will include trace-id propagation and a fallback_flag metric in all routed requests for observability. Redwood will also run a 50-prompt acceptance suite with Delta prior to go-live to measure delta in qualitative scoring.

2) SLA: Redwood will guarantee 99.8% availability for the specified tenant, with exclusions for force majeure, major cloud provider outages beyond Redwood's control, and scheduled maintenance (>=72 hours prior notice for maintenance windows). SLA credits will be limited to a percentage of the monthly invoice (language to be provided by Legal).

3) Enablement timeline: Redwood commits to an enablement window of 10 business days after the fully executed SOW to complete routing wiring, telemetry, and acceptance testing. Ops will perform a coordinated warm-up during week 2.

4) Acceptance tests and quality guardrails: If the acceptance suite indicates >15% degradation on critical prompts, Redwood and Delta will run a joint remediation plan; commercial remedies will be handled case-by-case.

I will share a concise SOW paragraph and runbook link by end of day Monday for Legal insertion. This captures the product/engineering guarantees and the escape rails.

—Priyom
Principal PM, Product — Redwood Inference
